title: 2012 HMMT February Algebra Problem 3
statement:
Given points \(a\) and \(b\) in the plane, let \(a \oplus b\) be the unique point \(c\) such that \(a b c\) is an equilateral triangle with \(a, b, c\) in the clockwise orientation.

Solve \((x \oplus(0,0)) \oplus(1,1)=(1,-1)\) for \(x\).

solutions.text: \(\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) It is clear from the definition of \(\oplus\) that \(b \oplus(a \oplus b)=a\) and if \(a \oplus b=c\) then \(b \oplus c=a\) and \(c \oplus a=b\). Therefore \(x \oplus(0,0)=(1,1) \oplus(1,-1)=(1-\sqrt{3}, 0)\). Now this means \(x=(0,0) \oplus(1-\sqrt{3}, 0)=\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\).
